newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Eurorand flood gives fresh fillip to S.Africa debt.
newsitem.headline: Eurorand flood gives fresh fillip to S.Africa debt.

text.p: A fresh flood of rand Eurobond issues underpinned an already bullish South African debt market on Thursday, taking long bond yields to their best levels since July 3, 1996.
The benchmark R150 issue was last yielding 14.80 percent, after touching 14.73 percent, helped by news that the government remains on track to deliver on its budget target in 1996/97.
Ben Hall, head of capital markets at Hambros in Johannesburg, said the day's nominal issuance of 800 million rand took total issues so far this year to 3.95 billion rand.

"It's a very good sign. What is particularly encouraging is the variety of issuance. We've had a one-year, two-year and 10-year zero today -- what it means is that the market is gaining depth," Hall said.
Hall said the 500 million rand 10-year zero-coupon Eurorand issue from the International Finance Corp -- the first of its kind -- would attract both retail and institutional demand.
"It shows there is a rich variety of investors in the market right now," he said.
In addition to traditional interest from investors in Germany, Switzerland and the Benelux countries, market participants said there was also increasing demand from Italy and the Far East.
Investors have been tempted back to South African debt by high coupons and the perception that the rand will stabilise in 1997 and recover some of the ground lost last year.
In addition to the IFC, Thursday also saw a 100 million rand one-year issue from Volkswagen Finance NV, lead managed by Chase, making its Eurorand debut.
Hebaba Finance issued a two-year 100 million rand bond and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development added 100 million to an earlier 100 million one-year issue.
